newsitem.title: UK: Britain warns Serbia not to obstruct protests.
newsitem.headline: Britain warns Serbia not to obstruct protests.

text.p: Britain on Monday warned Serbia not to obstruct opposition protests and said failure to abide by election results could harm its relations with the rest of the world.

A Foreign Office statement said Britain was "deeply concerned" by recent events in Serbia, where up to a quarter of a million people have braved police moves to deter protests and rallied daily calling for democracy.

"We call on the Serbian authorities not to obstruct opposition supporters from meeting and demonstrating peacefully, and to respect the human rights of all their citizens. All sides should refrain from acts of provocation and violence," it said.

Britain urged the Serbian authorities to abide by the results of local elections held on 17 November, which were won by the opposition but annulled by President Slobodan Milosevic on the basis of "irregularities".

The opposition parties, supported later by a special OSCE mission headed by former Spanish prime minister Felipe Gonzalez, accused the authorities of blatant vote fraud and demanded that its victories be reinstated.

"A failure by the Serbian authorities to respond quickly and positively to Mr Gonzalez's report will have a negative impact on Serbia's relations with the EU and the rest of the international community," the Foreign Office statement said.

Milosevic said last week that Serbia's fate would not be sealed by "a foreign hand" and he is yet to respond to last week's critical report by the OSCE, the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe.
Other Western governments have warned Milosevic he can forget about financial aid for Yugoslavia's wrecked economy unless he concedes electoral defeats and starts broad democratic reform.
